text:
That hamlet had a special way

of being:

the air fresher, cleaner, and everything,

everything was a landscape painted on glass!


For being soft and sweet, for being plaintive,

the birds' voices were almost a sigh...

And blue was the distant sierra, as though one saw it

behind a sapphire...


For the sadness of those paths,

the fragrant flowers had words;

and in the tamarind trees, with the clarineros,

zenzontles moaned, turtledoves wept...


The sun-gilded tile-roofed ranches

rose rough among the murmuring green of the cane,

and the lemon trees gave their velvet shadows

to the open balcony facing the mountains.


And you were the aloof, brown Pueblan girl;

and I was the traveler full of illusion;

and when you appeared, how lovely the happy morning became,

as if roses were springing from the balcony!...


And your loves were a raft of flowers,

brown girl, Pueblan girl, honey of the cane fields...

And my love was the water that wept in torrents

so the raft of flowers might float...

translation.title: Raft of Flowers
translation.editorial_note: “Clarineros” and “zenzontles” are retained as local bird names; the translation keeps the poem’s final water-and-flowers metaphor.
